svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Component · Blended clip row · approved · wide
svg.desc: Mirrors App/BlendedClipRow.swift (BlendedClipRow — ProjectDetailView's versionRow wraps it with the context menu and swipe-to-delete; the Gallery panel uses it too): thumbnail → ProjectThumbnailView (58×42), title → "Blended clip N · speed · length", subtitle → "fps · relative date", trailing "Open" → the result screen (model.openBlend), the whole row otherwise tapping to play. The plain case — no source-codec segment, no true-light flag. One row of the BLENDED CLIPS list; a card holds N of these stacked with no gap. See components/README.md for the full contract and the other rows (from-codec, true-light, sliced, on-picplace, not-available). 2026-09-26 (plan §12 + §16): the thumbnail wears the clip's holdings pill — BlendHoldingsPill → HoldingsPillBody (App/HoldingsPill.swift), .scaleEffect(0.8, anchor: .bottomTrailing).padding(2), i.e. 0.8 scale, 2 pt in from the thumbnail's bottom-right corner — here components/holdings-pill.blend.here.safe.svg: the clip on this device (green layers) and verified on PicPlace (the neutral ✓). The pill is the generated file's markup INLINED (mask ids prefixed), never redrawn by hand — re-copy it if holdings-pill.make.py changes the pill. Quick Look and browsers do not follow an <image> inside an <image>, which is why it is inlined: the pill travels with the row onto every screen that places it. A library never connected to PicPlace shows no pill on a clip that is here; ↑ (holdings-pill.blend.here.needs) while the clip is not up yet, amber ↑ while its project's heavy run sends it. The play.fill glyph (and amber disc) the pre-component mirrors drew over the thumbnail — README's "known gap": ProjectThumbnailView draws none — is gone from this file: the code never had it, and the pill now holds that corner. 2026-11-06 (docs/approved-assets.md): every row ends in the approve seal — ApproveToggle (App/ApprovedAssetViews.swift), a 28 pt hit area in the row's HStack(spacing: 12) between the text column and the trailing button: checkmark.seal 17 pt medium in secondary 70 % until the output is approved, checkmark.seal.fill in LL.accent after (the approved and edited.approved states); a press toggles. Here it is centred 72.5 pt in from the row's right edge, 12 pt before Open. The text column ends 12 pt before it (178.5 pt from x 84), so the same real strings clip sooner. THIS STATE: the default row once its output is approved for use — blends[].approvedAt is set; the seal is filled in LL.accent, nothing else moves.
